original_question: Let A be a sectorial operator on an L^p-space with p in (1, infinity), and assume that -A generates a positive C_0-semigroup. Must A then have a bounded H-infinity calculus, have bounded imaginary powers, or be R-analytic?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, read together with its equivalent reformulation in Proposition 1.2; Theorem 1.3 is the affirmative L^p special case that explains why your draft is phrased on an L^p-space.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the generator/sectorial-operator setting, the L^p model case, positivity of the semigroup, and the three regularity notions that the paper places next to each other: bounded H^∞-calculus, bounded imaginary powers, and R-analyticity.
missing_details: The paper’s main open formulation is on a complex UMD-Banach lattice X, not just on an L^p-space.
The semigroup hypothesis is stronger than positivity: -A must generate a positive contractive analytic C_0-semigroup.
Contractivity is part of the statement: T(t) must be contractive for every t >= 0 on the real line.
Analyticity is part of the statement: the semigroup must extend to a bounded holomorphic semigroup on some sector.
Because -A generates a bounded analytic C_0-semigroup, sectoriality of A is automatic; it is not the main extra hypothesis in the paper’s official formulation.
The paper’s primary semigroup-side conclusion is that the semigroup is R-analytic; this is a property of the semigroup, not of the operator A phrased directly.
In the equivalent operator-side reformulation, the relevant bounded H^∞-calculus is of angle strictly smaller than π/2.
Likewise, the bounded imaginary powers formulation is with the corresponding angle bound < π/2.
Theorem 1.3 already settles the L^p case affirmatively, so the genuine research question in the paper is the UMD-Banach lattice generalization, not the already-proved L^p statement.
The ambient scalar field is complex, by the paper’s standing convention.
If one keeps the L^p model case in view, the space should be written as L^p(Ω) for some measure space Ω with 1 < p < ∞.
refined_question: Let X be a complex UMD-Banach lattice, and let -A generate a positive contractive analytic C_0-semigroup on X. Must this semigroup be R-analytic?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, under the same hypotheses, must A admit a bounded H^∞-calculus—and hence bounded imaginary powers—of angle < π/2?
justification: The draft mixes the paper’s solved L^p model case with its actual open conjecture. Conjecture 1.1 is the research question; Proposition 1.2 is the nearby place where the paper reformulates that question in terms of bounded H^∞-calculus and bounded imaginary powers; and Theorem 1.3 gives the affirmative answer for L^p-spaces, which is why your draft mentions L^p and those stronger regularity properties. The missing words 'contractive' and 'analytic' are essential, and the paper’s intended ambient setting is a complex UMD-Banach lattice rather than merely an L^p-space.
